rationale:
**Applies.** `validate_query_placement` (src/sites.rs:392-428) is a repository-validation function. It takes a parameter named `errors` (`errors: &mut Vec<String>`) and pushes validation errors into it. It is not authoring code that collects errors only to abort. It is therefore a site of `requirements.ci.errors`.

**Obligations.** After one of its checks fails, a site must still run every later independent check, and it must not report one failure twice.

**Violation matches.**
- **Line 410, `continue` in the `let ... else` branch.** It runs when a line is not a query fence. No check has failed at that point; the line is just not a candidate. Skipping it is harmless.
- **Line 413, `continue` when the line starts inside a code block.** It also runs before any check fails, because code-block text is meant to stay literal. It skips only a non-candidate line. It does not skip any check that follows a failure.

**Whole function.**
- The only check is whether the query fence sits inside a `{req}` body. It runs for every candidate line, and a failure pushes an error and then continues the loop.
- No early exit follows a failed check. There is no `?` and no `return`. The loop never breaks.
- Each failing line pushes exactly one error, so no failure is reported twice.
- Each message starts with the location (`label:line`), names the check, and gives the query name and kind. That fits the validation-error definition.

The site has no gaps.

text: Repository validation MUST continue after a failed check and report every failed
check it finds in one run, each as a {term}`requirements.ci.validation_error`.
This is a convention for every validation error; the requirement for each check
states which conditions that check reports. A file that cannot be parsed, such as
a malformed `habeas.toml`, `book.toml`, or evidence file, is one failed check:
its error MAY report only the first parse or decoding problem in that file, and
checks that do not depend on its contents MUST still run.
The code that sequences the repository's checks carries out the first paragraph.
A repository-validation function that collects validation errors MUST hold them
in a parameter or local variable named `errors`, and a function with such a
variable is a site below; authoring code that collects errors only to abort is
not one. After one of its checks fails, a site MUST still run every later check
that does not depend on the failed check's result, including later checks in the
same loop iteration, and MUST NOT report one failure twice.
One message in a repository validation report, describing a single failed check.
